snapshot.text: Aena, the Spanish airport operator, ended FY2024 with revenue up {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} and EBITDA up {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}, while Fitch upgraded its long-term rating and Moody's moved its outlook to positive.
Net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{net_leverage@FY2024}}, helped by total debt down {{total_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{total_debt@FY2024}}.

The point to watch is liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} as cash and cash-like investments declined by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}.

credit_metrics.text: EBITDA rose by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}} and operating profit by {{operating_profit.change@FY2024}} to {{operating_profit@FY2024}}, lifting the EBITDA margin by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}.
Gross leverage fell by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2024}} and net debt was reduced by {{net_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{net_debt@FY2024}}.

Cash generation strengthened: FFO rose by {{ffo.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo@FY2024}}, taking FFO to debt up by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}}, and free cash flow rose by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}}.
FCF to debt rose by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}}, while interest coverage eased by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}.
Capex intensity fell by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}, which supported the rise in free cash flow.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2024}} to {{passengers@FY2024}}, although traffic growth slowed by {{traffic_growth.change@FY2024}} to {{traffic_growth@FY2024}}.

Aeronautical revenue per passenger rose by {{aero_revenue_per_passenger.change@FY2024}} to {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2024}}, with the CNMC setting the maximum adjusted annual revenue per passenger for 2025 unchanged versus the prior year.
The result for the year includes the gain on the sale of ADI's stake in ESSP SAS, and the Cartagena concession ended during the year.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}, and cash liquidity declined by the same amount to {{cash_liquidity@FY2024}}.
In FY2023 liquidity was {{liquidity@FY2023}}, including {{undrawn_facilities@FY2023}} of undrawn committed credit facilities, and liquidity to revenue was {{liquidity_to_revenue@FY2023}}.
Funding conditions improved during the year, with Fitch upgrading Aena's long-term and short-term ratings and Moody's moving the outlook to positive.

peer_positioning.text: Aena has the highest EBITDA margin among the airport peers ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@FY2024}}), at {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}} against a median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@FY2024}}.
Gross leverage sits in the middle of the group ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2024}}), with the company itself the median of the peer set.

Cash generation leads the group: FFO to debt of {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}} and FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}} both rank {{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2024}} and {{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2024}} against medians of {{ffo_to_debt.peer_median@FY2024}} and {{fcf_to_debt.peer_median@FY2024}}.

Interest coverage of {{interest_coverage@FY2024}} is the strongest of the group ({{interest_coverage.peer_rank@FY2024}}) against a median of {{interest_coverage.peer_median@FY2024}}, and capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2024}} is below the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2024}}.

watch_items.text: Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} as cash and cash-like investments were drawn down by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}}.
Coverage: interest coverage eased by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, a weaker move than the rest of the credit profile.
Traffic: growth slowed by {{traffic_growth.change@FY2024}} to {{traffic_growth@FY2024}}, so the pace of passenger expansion is moderating.
Regulation: the CNMC set the maximum adjusted annual revenue per passenger for 2025 unchanged versus the prior year, which limits tariff-led revenue growth.
